data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The candidate bound W(C) = c_{n-1} + c_n is insufficient to guarantee canonicity, refuted by the coin system C = (25, 10, 1) where the smallest counterexample is 30, strictly exceeding the bound of 11.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The refutation would fail if the greedy representation of 30 for C = (25, 10, 1) was optimal or tied with the 3-coin representation, which it is not.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The refutation would fail if the bound W(C) was defined differently, such as W(C) = c_1 + c_2, under which 30 < 35 would not constitute a refutation.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the system C = (25, 10, 1) were canonical, there would be no counterexample to find, but it is demonstrably non-canonical.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"For the strictly decreasing coin system C = (25, 10, 1), the proposed bound yields W(C) = c_{n-1} + c_n = 10 + 1 = 11. However, the amount w = 30 requires 6 coins using the greedy algorithm (one 25 and five 1s), while the optimal representation uses three 10s (3 coins). Since 30 > 11, checking only amounts up to W(C) would fail to find this counterexample, proving the bound W(C) = c_{n-1} + c_n universally invalid.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
